title: Reasons for Attrition in Foster Parenting Scheme and Proposed Guidelines for Co-parenting Arrangements for Fostering
what_it_is: Reasons for Attrition in Foster Parenting Scheme and Proposed Guidelines for Co-parenting Arrangements for Fostering

sections.label: Foster parent shortfall and attrition
sections.summary: Questions ask about the estimated shortfall of foster parents, their attrition rate, reasons for it, and planned programmes and resolutions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) what the present estimated shortfall of foster parents is; and (b) what additional programmes are planned to address this shortfall, if any.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) what has been the attrition rate of foster parents in the last three years; (b) what are the reasons or issues for such attrition; and (c) how can these issues be resolved.

sections.label: Foster parent deregistration rate
sections.summary: About 6% of foster parents have been deregistered each year on average over the last three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: On attrition, about 6% of foster parents have been deregistered each year on average over the last three years.

sections.label: Monthly fostering allowance
sections.summary: Foster parents receive a monthly fostering allowance of $1,100 to $1,800 depending on the child's age and needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: Foster parents receive a monthly fostering allowance ranging from $1,100 to $1,800, depending on the child’s age and needs, to help defray childcare and other out-of-pocket expenses.

sections.label: Digital access for foster parents
sections.summary: MSF is working to enhance foster parents' experience by providing access to the foster child's education and healthcare information through HealthHub and Parents Gateway.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: This is also the feedback consistent with what we have gotten from many foster parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: Therefore, MSF is currently working to further enhance our foster parents' experience by providing them access to the foster child's education and healthcare information through HealthHub and Parents Gateway.

sections.label: Monitoring after reintegration
sections.summary: Children are monitored for at least 12 months after reintegration, and longer depending on family circumstances and assessed risk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: Children are also monitored for at least 12 months after reintegration and longer if we need to, depending on the family circumstances and the overall assessed level of risk.

sections.label: Digital appointment booking access
sections.summary: The digital access being worked on will allow appointment booking and updates to be available for foster parents to access.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: Yes, indeed, so, the digital access that we are working on will allow for the appointment booking system and updates to be made available for foster parents to access.
